cues: Nothing can happen until there is a cambial ring, so first the ray cells dedifferentiate.
Then the new cambium makes secondary xylem.
As the wood builds up, the primary phloem is crushed.
Only once the cortex is stretched does the cork cambium form and make lenticels.
And tyloses come last of all, in old wood turning into heartwood.
text: Think it through. Nothing can happen until there is a cambial ring, so first the ray cells dedifferentiate. That event creates the meristem. Then the new cambium makes secondary xylem. As the wood builds up, the primary phloem is crushed. Only once the cortex is stretched does the cork cambium form and make lenticels. And tyloses come last of all, in old wood turning into heartwood.
